newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - NAB still seeking acquisitions.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - NAB still seeking acquisitions.

text.p: National Australia Bank Ltd, the nation's largest and most profitable bank with operations in the United Kingdom, United States, and Asia, said on Thursday that it was still on the lookout for acquisitions.
"We are still keen to seek more acquisitions and alliances," managing director Don Argus told reporters.
NAB earlier reported a 6.8 percent rise in 1995/96 (October/September) net profit to A$2.10 billion.
Argus also said NAB had scope for further cost-cutting. "The opportunity to dip into our costs are boundless," he said.
Argus was non-committal about any further mergers in Australia while the Wallis inquiry into further deregulation of the banking sector was underway.
"Frankly, I don't have any idea on what is going to come out of it, but there is a much bigger gain out there of organic growth and that is what these results are all about," he said.
The Wallis inquiry is due to hand its final report to the Australian government by March next year.
NAB is the largest single shareholder in regional bank St George Bank Ltd with a 7.8 percent stake and analysts believe NAB will launch a bid once the inquiry is over.
